material_units.source_text: Finite MDP, stationary policies $\pi,\pi'$. Write $P_{\pi'}(s,s')=\sum_a\pi'(a\mid s)P(s'\mid s,a)$ (row-stochastic, acting on value vectors; Section 2 used its transpose), $r_{\pi'}(s)=\sum_a\pi'(a\mid s)r(s,a)$ and $\bar a(s)=\sum_a\pi'(a\mid s)A^\pi(s,a)$. (a) Show that $\bar a=r_{\pi'}+\gamma P_{\pi'}V^\pi-V^\pi$. (b) Deduce $V^{\pi'}-V^\pi=(I-\gamma P_{\pi'})^{-1}\bar a$, and from it the performance difference lemma with its factor $\frac{1}{1-\gamma}$. (c) Two states $\{0,1\}$, deterministic actions stay and switch, reward 1 per step in state 1, $\gamma=\tfrac12$, start in state 0. $\pi$ switches with probability $\tfrac12$ in both states; $\pi'$ switches in state 0 and stays in state 1. Compute $A^\pi$, $\bar a$, $d^{\pi'}$ and $d^\pi$, check the lemma, and explain why the surrogate $L_\pi(\pi')$ happens to be exact here.

material_units.source_text:
(a) $\sum_a\pi'(a\mid s)Q^\pi(s,a)=\sum_a\pi'(a\mid s)\big[r(s,a)+\gamma\sum_{s'}P(s'\mid s,a)V^\pi(s')\big]=r_{\pi'}(s)+\gamma(P_{\pi'}V^\pi)(s)$; subtract $V^\pi(s)=\sum_a\pi'(a\mid s)V^\pi(s)$.
            (b) The Bellman equation of $\pi'$ is $V^{\pi'}=r_{\pi'}+\gamma P_{\pi'}V^{\pi'}$. Subtract $V^\pi$ and add and subtract $\gamma P_{\pi'}V^\pi$: $V^{\pi'}-V^\pi=\underbrace{r_{\pi'}+\gamma P_{\pi'}V^\pi-V^\pi}_{=\bar a}+\gamma P_{\pi'}(V^{\pi'}-V^\pi)$. Since $\|\gamma P_{\pi'}\|_\infty=\gamma\lt1$, $I-\gamma P_{\pi'}$ is invertible with Neumann series $\sum_t\gamma^tP_{\pi'}^t$, so $V^{\pi'}-V^\pi=(I-\gamma P_{\pi'})^{-1}\bar a$. Multiply by $\mu^{\top}$: $J(\pi')-J(\pi)=\mu^{\top}(I-\gamma P_{\pi'})^{-1}\bar a=\sum_t\gamma^t(\mu^{\top}P_{\pi'}^t)\bar a$, and $\mu^{\top}P_{\pi'}^t$ is the law of $s_t$ under $\pi'$, so $(1-\gamma)\sum_t\gamma^t\mu^{\top}P_{\pi'}^t=(d^{\pi'})^{\top}$. Hence $J(\pi')-J(\pi)=\frac{1}{1-\gamma}\sum_sd^{\pi'}(s)\bar a(s)$. Only the two Bellman equations were used; the telescoping proof of Section 1 is the same Neumann series read along trajectories.
            (c) $P_\pi=\tfrac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$, $r_\pi=(0,1)$, so $V^\pi=(I-\tfrac12P_\pi)^{-1}r_\pi=(0.5,\,1.5)$ and $J(\pi)=0.5$. Then $Q^\pi(0,\cdot)=(0.25,0.75)$ and $Q^\pi(1,\cdot)=(1.75,1.25)$ for (stay, switch), so $A^\pi(0,\cdot)=(-0.25,+0.25)$, $A^\pi(1,\cdot)=(+0.25,-0.25)$. $\pi'$ picks the positive-advantage action in both states: $\bar a=(0.25,0.25)$. Under $\pi'$ the chain is $0\to1\to1\to\dots$: $V^{\pi'}=(1,2)$, $J(\pi')=1$, $d^{\pi'}=(\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$, and indeed $\frac{1}{1-\gamma}\langle d^{\pi'},\bar a\rangle=2\cdot0.25=0.5=J(\pi')-J(\pi)$; also $(I-\tfrac12P_{\pi'})^{-1}\bar a=(0.5,0.5)=V^{\pi'}-V^\pi$. Under $\pi$: $d^\pi=(0.75,0.25)$, and $L_\pi(\pi')=2\langle d^\pi,\bar a\rangle=0.5$ as well. The surrogate's error is $\frac{1}{1-\gamma}\sum_s(d^{\pi'}-d^\pi)(s)\,\bar a(s)$; here $\bar a$ is constant and $\sum_s(d^{\pi'}-d^\pi)(s)=0$, so the error vanishes. The surrogate is wrong only through the correlation between where the state distribution moves and where the advantage is large, which is what the bound of Section 2 controls with $\epsilon^{\pi'}$.
